messages:
dana: heads up — I pushed the kernel-picker change to prefer int8-friendly GEMM for Llama mix after the batcher update, saw a small perf regression on GQA workloads this morning
alex: saw that too, was debugging — which workload? full Qwen/T5?
dana: spotted on our GQA-heavy suite (long-context chat sim), throughput dropped ~35% for some bundles. MQA runs seemed fine.
maria: can you paste the microprofile? guessing it's KV path related — maybe paged-kv fragmentation causing extra memcpy.
dana: here’s the quick perf dump from the repro run: 
```
workload: gqa_chat_long_2048
model: mixtral-8x7b (mqa variant)
baseline kernel pick: fast_gemm_f32
new kernel pick: int8_gemv_fused
throughput: 1768 tok/s -> 1145 tok/s
latency p95: 92ms -> 168ms
kv-hit-rate: 0.83 -> 0.78
page-evicts/sec: 0.0 -> 12.4
```

alex: page-evicts/sec jumping is a smoking gun. int8 path might be changing KV layout alignment or head packing. MQA vs GQA differences in num_key_value_heads could affect fragmentation.
ryan: do we have offline traces that show which allocation triggered evicts? can we repro with `KV_PAGED_DEBUG=1`?
maria: ran that locally, attaching a tiny snippet of the heap trace — looks like slabs of 3x head_size leftover per shard -> leftover small fragments that don't align with new kernel’s contiguous copy path.
ops-bot: incident: kernel-picker-rollback? created rollback branch redwood/kernel-fix-2419
dana: I tried a local quick-fix: force kernel-picker to prefer `aligned_gemm` when model.num_key_value_heads % 8 != 0. Re-ran, throughput back to 1710 tok/s, evicts dropped to 0.8/sec.
alex: interesting — so the int8_gemv_fused path assumes head packing like `heads % 8 == 0` and uses a fast memcpy that reads/writes 128B lanes. If heads not aligned, we do per-head stride copies which cause page-churn.
maria: next steps: 1) add alignment check into kernel selection heuristics 2) add a fallback that uses blocked-copy path when `kv_dim % 256 != 0` 3) add a batching heuristic tweak to avoid mixing MQA and GQA in same batch when possible.
dryan: +1. Also want a perf unit test that simulates a paged-KV fragmentation pattern: random slab frees to emulate long-tail chat.
dana: I can author the unit test — will add a `kv_paging_fragmentation_test` to eng-runtime/perf with paramized `num_key_value_heads` and `kv_dim`. Will include MQA/GQA combos.
alex: for telemetry, add a metric `kv_fragmentation_score` (0-1) from our allocator: (#free_fragments * avg_frag_size) / total_kv_mem. Alert threshold 0.12.
maria: one more observation — RoPE scaling changes in newer model variant increased sequence length handling, shifted sequence-length distribution which increased prefix cache pressure; that likely amplified the frag. So might want to recommend client-side prefix folding in addition to runtime fixes.
dana: filed ticket INF-3145 with repro script, perf logs, and patch diff. Will open PR for kernel-picker guard tomorrow.
ryan: thanks — if you need a quick review ping me, I can run the dedicated pool smoke tests.
ops-bot: deploy-check queued: pr/kerpick-guard-2419 -> smoke pool 5
dana: noted. tl;dr: regression caused by kernel selection mismatch with non-8-aligned KV head packing -> paged-KV fragmentation -> evicts -> throughput drop. Fix: alignment-aware kernel heuristic + batching isolation + perf tests. :thumbsup:
